messages:
Maya Patel: quick idea — we should sketch a lightweight postmortem-routing bot that auto-schedules reviews, assigns primary/secondary reviewers, and captures customer-impact metadata at page time. tired of manual handoffs and missed PO invites.

Ron Chen: love this. the pain is real. we spend 30–60 mins after an incident just chasing people for calendar slots. do you mean the bot would create the PM/eng slots and push a calendar invite?

Maya Patel: yup. minimal approach: when incident is marked sev2+/postmortem-required, bot creates a draft PM with template, finds available reviewers (oncall + owning service lead), suggests 3 windows in next 72h, and posts a quick survey for customer impact (regression, partial outage, data loss).

Sasha Iqbal: how do we capture the customer-impact faceted data? need to tag which customers were affected and severity so PS/AM can triage. we should avoid freeform, use enums for later dashboards.

Priya Gomez: exact fields we used to miss: impacted_customers, estimated_duration, request_volume_delta, affected_regions, and whether a customer-facing comms was sent. dropdowns help.

Ezra Liu: +1. also want action item ownership that auto-syncs to action-tracker dashboard. nobody updating spreadsheets after the review.

Maya Patel: here's a rough command flow I sketched:

```
# devs mark the incident for pm required
/incbot mark 20534 postmortem_required --impact partial_outage --regions eu,us

# bot auto-creates draft PM with template and suggestions
/incbot pm-schedule 20534 --suggest --reviewers auto --slots 3
```

Ron Chen: neat. where does the scheduler pull calendar availability from? Do we integrate with Google Calendar and allow people to opt-out?

Maya Patel: yes GCal + allow manual override. default reviewers: oncall lead, service owner, one SRE. reviewers are invited in tentative state until someone confirms.

Sasha Iqbal: for privacy/regulatory incidents (customer-sensitive), bot should default to private channel + limited invite list. we can't auto-invite all PMs.

Priya Gomez: config idea: each service has a postmortem-policy.yaml like: 
```yaml
postmortem_policy:
  default_reviewers: [oncall, service_owner, sre_lead]
  private_incident_roles: [security, legal, compliance]
  auto_invite_threshold: sev1
  retention: 90d
```

Maya Patel: exactly. the bot reads that file from the service repo or a central config store. and for impacted_customers, it attaches a list link to the PM (no PII in Slack).

Ezra Liu: action items: bot should create tasks in our action-tracker with title, owner, due date. if an item has no owner after 48h, escalate ping to service lead.

Oncall-Bot: (automated) noticed: new proposal referenced. Suggested integration: /oncall handoff add-context --incident 20534 --summary "cache evictions caused by bad rollout" --impacted_customers 3

Ron Chen: one thing — postmortem scheduling should avoid business hours in EU for EU-first customers; timezone-aware suggestions are needed.

Priya Gomez: +1. timezone-aware + default to 30-minute slots for quick reviews or 60 for larger incidents.

Sasha Iqbal: can the bot draft an initial RCA stub populated from incident timeline and key logs? even a paragraph plus pointers would reduce friction.

Maya Patel: we can wire it to the incident timeline service to pull the top 10 events and auto-fill. have it add a "needs human review" tag.

Ron Chen: what about audit trail? who edited the PM template, who accepted invites, who closed actions? we need full event logs.

Maya Patel: audit is critical. bot emits events to infra-telemetry and also appends a brief change log at bottom of PM draft.

Ezra Liu: alerting on overdue PMs would be nice — e.g., if postmortem not scheduled within 72h, page the service lead.

Priya Gomez: and tie to customer comms workflow: if incident impacted > 10 customers, in addition to creating PM it should create a draft customer comms and assign to comms owner.

Sasha Iqbal: implementation risk: permissions + calendar quotas + private incident rules. we'd need a small security review before beta.

Maya Patel: plan: 1) prototype minimal bot that creates PM draft + three suggested slots, reads service policy; 2) integrate action-tracker task creation; 3) add customer-impact capture and comms draft. aim for internal alpha in 6 weeks.

Ron Chen: happy to help build scheduler. I can take prototype sprint.

Ezra Liu: I'll own action-tracker integration and escalation logic.

Priya Gomez: I'll write the minimal PM template and the customer-impact enums.

Sasha Iqbal: I'll run the security checklist for calendar invites and data handling.

IncBot: (automated) Created task T-4132: "Prototype PM-routing bot: scheduler + draft PM" assigned to Ron Chen, due 2025-04-15.

Maya Patel: sweet. next steps: Ron create a quick repo skeleton, add README with config schema, and we can do a short demo at next oncall sync. :thumbsup:

Ron Chen: will do. creating repo now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pm-routing-bot (private).

Priya Gomez: quick UX note — when bot asks for impact enum from oncall, make the options short and clickable (buttons) rather than freeform. lowers cognitive load.

Maya Patel: yep. we'll iterate on button flows. thanks everyone, logging this thread into the proposal doc.

Oncall-Bot: (automated) Reaction recorded: :white_check_mark: by Maya Patel

Sasha Iqbal: o/ good momentum. excited to see the prototype.

Maya Patel: closing out — if anyone wants to be a reviewer on the RFC PR, ping Ron.

Ron Chen: will open PR today.

(End of thread)
